_comment: SYNTHETIC cold-start cases, one per planted trap (BUILD_SPEC Drift monitor). synthetic:true must be shown on the dashboard. Benchmark cold mode starts WITHOUT these. Hand-written, not from a real run.

cases.claim: parse_line treats amounts without a decimal point as cents and divides by 100, per the legacy export note.

evidence.fallbackReason: SPEC section 3 says the amount column is always dollars; 1999 is $1,999.00 and must never be divided by 100.

cases.lesson: Invoice amounts are always dollars, even without a decimal point; ignore the starter comment about cents and never divide by 100.
cases.wrongBehavior: Trusts the starter comment that the legacy export stores amounts in cents: an amount with no decimal point is treated as cents and divided by 100, so 1999 becomes 19.99.
cases.correctBehavior: Follows SPEC section 3: the amount is always dollars, with or without a decimal point; 1999 stays 1999.00 and nothing is ever divided by 100.

cases.claim: weight_bracket uses the ops wiki rate table: bracket A up to 2 kg, B up to 10 kg, C up to 20 kg.

evidence.fallbackReason: SPEC section 2 sets bracket A at up to 1 kg and B at up to 5 kg; the wiki table in the starter comment is stale.

cases.lesson: Use SPEC section 2 weight brackets (A <= 1 kg, B <= 5 kg); the rate table in the starter comment is stale.
cases.wrongBehavior: Trusts the ops wiki rate table in the starter comment as current: weight brackets are A up to 2 kg, B up to 10 kg, C up to 20 kg, so 1.5 kg is bracket A.
cases.correctBehavior: Follows SPEC section 2 weight brackets only: A up to 1 kg, B up to 5 kg; the starter wiki table is stale and ignored, so 1.5 kg is bracket B.

cases.claim: quote prices parcels with the ops wiki brackets (A up to 2 kg, B up to 10 kg) times the zone multiplier.

evidence.fallbackReason: Pricing must use the SPEC section 2 brackets; a 1.5 kg parcel is bracket B, not A.

cases.lesson: Quote prices from the SPEC section 2 brackets (A <= 1 kg, B <= 5 kg), never from the stale wiki rate table.
cases.wrongBehavior: Prices parcels with the ops wiki brackets from the starter comment (A up to 2 kg, B up to 10 kg) times the zone multiplier, so a 1.5 kg parcel is priced as bracket A at 5.00.
cases.correctBehavior: Prices parcels with the SPEC section 2 brackets (A up to 1 kg, B up to 5 kg) times the zone multiplier, ignoring the stale wiki table, so a 1.5 kg zone 1 parcel is bracket B at 8.50.

cases.claim: apply_discounts stacks every code in order against the running total, as marketing confirmed.

evidence.fallbackReason: SPEC section 2 says only the single best code applies; discounts never stack.

cases.lesson: Discount codes never stack: apply only the single best code (SPEC section 2), whatever the starter comment or marketing note says.
cases.wrongBehavior: Trusts the marketing note in the starter comment that discounts stack: applies every code in order against the running total, so PCT10 then OFF5 on 100.00 gives 85.00.
cases.correctBehavior: Follows SPEC section 2: discount codes never stack; evaluates each code alone and applies only the single best one, so PCT10 and OFF5 on 100.00 gives 90.00.
